note: Department of Agriculture (DA) El Niño farm-damage reports as published by news outlets, gathered by hand on 2026-11-14 to compare with the satellite record. Only short quotes are kept; read the full articles at the URLs. The sha256 is of the page HTML as fetched that day and documents what was read; news pages change, so it will not match a later fetch. Figures are early-season bulletins, not final totals.

reports.title: El Niño agriculture damage climbs to P6.3 billion
reports.quote: DA spokesman Arnel de Mesa said Mimaropa remains the most affected region, with damage placed at P1.7 billion followed by Western Visayas, with P1.5 billion, and Cordillera Administrative Region, P800 million.

reports.title: El Niño farm damage hits P5.9 billion
reports.quote: The hardest-hit province was Iloilo, where losses were valued at between P500 million and P600 million, followed by Palawan at P350 million to P500 million.

reports.title: El Niño damage to agriculture nears P4 billion — DA
reports.quote: In its El Niño bulletin, the DA said the estimated damage to the farm sector in 11 regions — Cordillera Administrative Region, Ilocos Region, Cagayan Valley, Central Luzon, Calabarzon, MIMAROPA, Bicol Region, Western Visayas, Zamboanga Peninsula, Davao Region, and Soccsksargen — stood at P3.94 billion, affecting 73,713 farmers and fisherfolk as of April 16.

regions.reported: Most affected region, P1.7 billion; Palawan second-hardest-hit province
Second most affected, P1.5 billion; Iloilo hardest-hit province

reports.title: Agricultural damage caused by El Niño reaches P464 million
reports.quote: The affected regions are: Mimaropa, Zamboanga Peninsula, Northern Mindanao, Davao Region, Soccsksargen, Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao

reports.title: Agricultural damage from El Niño rises to P1.33 billion
reports.quote: According to the report, however, Northern Mindanao has been bearing the brunt of El Niño.
